meta.title: Pricing
meta.description: Transparent pricing for engineering support and project engagements.

intro.label: Pricing
intro.heading: Transparent by design.
intro.sub: One rate ladder, two ways to use it: hourly support and fixed-price projects. The longer you commit, the lower the rate. No hidden fees. All prices are exclusive of VAT — EU reverse charge applies for cross-border B2B transactions.

categories.title: Rates
categories.model: Per hour · set by your commitment
categories.desc: Three rates, set by how long you commit. After the assessment, your rate applies to support and fixed-price projects alike — across all your installations.
categories.callout: Systems not built by Imbra start with a separate ad-hoc assessment — from €800 (one day) — before any commitment. Commitments and fixed prices are quoted from it.

terms.label: Committed hours
terms.value: Cover support or projects, are billed whether used or not, and expire each month

notes: Reserved capacity is limited; commitments are accepted in order of signing.
24/7 on-call is an optional add-on to the Annual tier and is quoted separately.
Response times, service levels, and expenses are defined in the Master Service Agreement; scheduling, scope, and deployment responsibilities in each Statement of Work.

categories.title: Engineering Support
categories.desc: Escalation support for industrial software systems — the level your own team or vendor calls when they are stuck: incident investigation, root cause analysis, hotfixes, workaround guidance, documentation, and technical exploration.

terms.label: Out-of-hours
terms.value: 1.5× your rate — evenings after 18:00 CET, weekends, public holidays

categories.title: Project Engagement
categories.model: Fixed price = estimated hours × your rate
desc: Refactoring, new features, migrations, and integrations. The system assessment (see 1) produces the hour estimate; multiplied by your rate, it is the fixed price — written in the Statement of Work before work starts.

The project consumes its estimated hours, not the hours actually worked: if Imbra's estimate was too low, Imbra absorbs the difference, and the price moves only if the scope does. A project of at least 20 hours per month over three months or more earns the Quarterly rate on its own.

items.title: Small company — one legacy system
items.desc: Quarterly term, renewed for a year. Two-day assessment of a mid-sized legacy test framework, then support at the minimum volume.

items.title: Large company — 100 installations
items.desc: Annual term at 80 hours a month. Four-week assessment of a complex system estate, then support covering every installation under one agreement.

items.title: Project — small integration
items.desc: No commitment. One-day assessment, then an 80-hour integration bridging two systems.

items.title: Project — runtime migration
items.desc: Quarterly term. A 400-hour project over four months, run with the client's own team — three-day assessment, then migration off an unsupported runtime.

items.title: Emergency — business hours
items.desc: No commitment. 8-hour engagement on an already-assessed system, on a weekday, subject to availability.

items.title: Emergency — weekend
items.desc: No commitment. 8-hour engagement on an already-assessed system, on a Saturday, subject to availability.

legalNote: Full terms, including service levels, are defined in the Master Service Agreement.
